title: The Horizon of Cape Reckoning
premise: Ines Marchetti, a debt-ridden storm chaser on the fog-bound coast of Cape Reckoning, shelters a dying prospector who trades him a map to the wreck of the Meridian for a promise: deliver the salvage to the prospector's estranged daughter, not the creditors circling both their names. Racing a six-tide deadline against the ruthless Calloway salvage fleet, Ines assembles a ragtag crew of castoffs who become the family none of them had. Betrayed by his own creditor and nearly drowned in the final storm, Ines reaches the wreck first, honors the promise over profit, and finds that justice outside the law costs everything except what matters.
about_author: Edmund Yarrow is the pen name of a former merchant sailor who spent eleven years running supply runs along the North Atlantic coast before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage, where he claims the weather does half the plotting.

chapters.title: The Debt of Optimists
chapters.summary: Ines Marchetti, POV. Ines chases a squall along the Cape Reckoning cliffs to photograph it for a client, then returns to find his boat impounded by Voss, the cheerful loan shark who owns his debts. The chapter establishes Ines's skill, his desperation, and the ticking clock of what he owes. Emotional beat: pride curdling into dread.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. During the night a soaked, wounded old man collapses against Ines's door — a prospector named Aldous Wren, pursued by men from the Calloway fleet. Ines hides him despite knowing Voss would pay handsomely to know where he is. Emotional beat: instinctive decency overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Map and the Promise
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Feverish and dying, Wren shows Ines a hand-drawn map to the Meridian, a wreck holding salvage worth a fortune, and makes him swear an oath: the salvage goes to Wren's daughter Mara, not to any fleet or creditor. Ines swears before understanding what it will cost. Emotional beat: the weight of a promise given too easily.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Wren dies at dawn; the tide tables show the wreck's window closes in six tides when the channel silts. Ines learns the Calloway fleet has the same map fragment and is provisioning to sail within two days. He must find a crew he cannot pay. Emotional beat: grief converted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Crew Nobody Wanted
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Ines recruits a disgraced harbor pilot named Odile, a teenage runaway mechanic called Finch, and Bram, a gentle giant blacklisted from every crew in port. Each joins for reasons of their own wounds rather than wages. Emotional beat: strangers recognizing kinship in damage.

chapters.title: Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Voss offers to forgive Ines's entire debt if he delivers the wreck's location to the Calloway fleet instead. The offer is genuinely tempting — freedom on paper. Ines refuses without explaining why, even to himself. Emotional beat: the first quiet test of the promise.

chapters.title: Out Past the Light
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew slips out of harbor at night, dodging a Calloway spotter boat. Odile navigates the treacherous Serrated Reach by memory and nerve while Finch keeps the temperamental engine alive. They clear the cape as dawn breaks. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by how much lies ahead.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A becalmed day becomes a night of stories; Bram reveals he lost a family to a company that valued cargo over lives, which is why he sails with Ines. The crew begins functioning as something more than hired hands. Emotional beat: found family taking root.

chapters.title: The First Tide Turns
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They reach the first waypoint and find a Calloway buoy already anchored there — the fleet is ahead of schedule. Ines realizes someone leaked their departure time. Suspicion falls on Finch, who has been secretive about her past. Emotional beat: trust cracking under pressure.

chapters.title: Finch's Secret
chapters.summary: Finch's POV. Confronted, Finch confesses she is Wren's granddaughter by his other child — she recognized the map and stowed her hope inside the voyage. She never betrayed them; the leak was the harbormaster, paid by Voss. Emotional beat: accusation giving way to deeper bonds.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Barometers plummet; a named storm is bending toward the cape, exactly the kind Ines has chased his whole life but never sailed into. The crew must choose: shelter and lose two tides, or run the outer passage through the storm's edge. Emotional beat: fear weighed against the promise.

chapters.title: The Edge of the Storm
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They take the outer passage. Ines reads the sky like scripture, calling wind shifts seconds before they hit, and the crew follows him into chaos because he is certain. They survive, barely, losing part of their stores. Emotional beat: Ines transformed from debtor to leader.

chapters.title: Mara Wren
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On the far shore, Mara Wren — a salvage lawyer fighting Calloway in court and losing — receives word that a dying stranger sent a crew to find her. Skeptical of sentiment, she charters a fast skiff to intercept them. Emotional beat: guarded hope she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Anchor
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the second waypoint, Voss himself arrives on a Calloway tender, having bought the harbormaster's information outright. He offers Ines one last chance and, refused, takes Bram hostage as insurance. The crew must sail on leaving their friend behind. Emotional beat: rage and helplessness entwined.

chapters.title: Two Tides Left
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Held aboard the Calloway flagship, Bram stalls his interrogators with patience and silence while quietly mapping the ship's weaknesses. Meanwhile Ines's crew races the silting channel, down a man and short on supplies. Emotional beat: endurance as its own kind of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Drowned Cathedral
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. With one tide remaining they find the Meridian, resting in a submerged sea cave like a drowned cathedral. Diving in near-zero visibility, Ines locates the strongroom — and discovers the salvage includes documents proving Calloway sank the ship deliberately decades ago. Emotional beat: awe turning cold with implication.

chapters.title: The Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The Calloway fleet converges on the cave mouth as the last tide begins to fall. Voss offers to trade Bram for the salvage. Ines must decide whether the promise was to deliver treasure — or justice. Emotional beat: the promise reinterpreted at gunpoint.

chapters.title: The Devil's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines trades the strongroom's gold for Bram, secretly keeping the documents. As the tide drops, the cave entrance narrows, trapping the fleet's largest ship inside with them. Finch rigs the Meridian's old boilers to blow the cave's secondary channel open. Emotional beat: desperate ingenuity as defiance.

chapters.title: Six Tides Spent
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. The explosion opens the channel just as the storm's trailing edge hits; in the chaos, Mara's skiff arrives and her evidence turns Calloway's own escort officers against the flagship. Voss, caught between mutiny and the collapsing cave, loses everything he came for. Emotional beat: catharsis earned through every prior sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Was Promised
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ashore, Ines gives Mara the documents and Wren's letter, refusing any share of the gold beyond clearing his debts. Mara, moved by a promise kept when no one was watching, ensures the courts finish what the storm started. Emotional beat: love beginning where duty ends.

chapters.title: The Horizon of Cape Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Voss is arrested; Calloway collapses under scandal. Ines, debt-free for the first time in years, stands at the cape with his crew — no longer a crew, but a family — watching a storm build on the horizon, this time chasing it for joy. Emotional beat: freedom finally understood.

chapters.title: Tides to Come
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. Months later, the refitted boat sails under a new name — the Aldous Wren — with Odile piloting, Finch engineering, Bram at the rail, and Mara aboard as partner. Ines receives a letter hinting at another wreck, another promise waiting. Emotional beat: an ending that opens like a door.
